Ankeny Liquor Dollars: Hy-Vee vs Costco vs All Other Stores

Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 10:49 AM CDT · orders through Aug 31, 2026

“Costco arrived in Ankeny in 2023 I think, so show monthly liquor dollars in Ankeny: Hy-Vee vs Costco vs all other stores, next 6 months, but have all charts start in year 2017”

Read as All liquor products · Ankeny, Iowa (all stores) · dollars per month · Sep 2026 to Feb 2027 · one forecast per store group: hy-vee, costco, all other stores (3)

Why it was read this way
  • Place is the city of Ankeny, Iowa; includes all stores located there.
  • Breakout splits stores into three series: those with 'Hy-Vee' in the name, those with 'Costco' in the name, and all remaining Ankeny stores combined.
  • Costco's Ankeny store opened in late 2022, so its history starts then; this does not affect the forecast logic.
  • Measure is total sales dollars (gross order value), not profit.
  • Horizon is the next 6 full calendar months after August 2026 (September 2026 through February 2027), per the default since no horizon was stated.
  • Grain is monthly, as not otherwise specified beyond 'monthly' which was explicitly requested.
  • Charts display history starting in 2017 per the request, though all data from 2016 is included in the underlying calculation.

Ankeny liquor sales are forecast at $6.12 million over the next six months, down 7% from the same months last year. This forecast is 18% more accurate than simply repeating last year's outcome.

  • Tuning (Sep 2022 to Aug 2024): every month through these months, each candidate model was trained on all months before that point and forecast the next 6, and its forecasts were compared with what actually sold. 48 distinct configurations of ridge regression and LightGBM were compared, differing in targets, inputs and history lengths, and the settings with the smallest misses were picked: a ridge regression.
  • Testing (Sep 2024 to Aug 2026): the picked settings forecast months they never saw; this is where the accuracy figures come from. Every month the model was retrained on all months before that point and forecast the next 6, 19 times in all, each scored against what actually sold. Dotted orange is those forecasts, 1 to 6 months ahead (pick above the chart).
  • Forecast (Sep 2026 to Feb 2027): tuning is repeated on the Testing period, so the forecast uses the most recent data. The re-tuned model, a ridge regression, is retrained on everything through Aug 2026 and forecasts ahead.
  • Green band (80% range): inferred by comparing the model's forecasts with actual sales in the Testing period; it spans the middle 80% of those misses.

How far to trust it

Every month in the Testing period was forecast by a model trained only on earlier months, then compared with what actually happened and with the simplest serious baseline: the same month last year.

How the data was prepared

Monthly dollars from Jan 2016 through Aug 2026. The AI wrote the SQL query that selects the sales records for this request; fixed code adds them up, and every other step is fixed code that runs the same way for every request. The code itself was written in advance with Claude Code, with a person reviewing and approving every data fix.

what was donedone by
Before any request: building the warehouse (once, with load_data.py)
Loaded every sales record the state published since 2016 into Postgres: text turned into real dates and numbers, each record given its own id, and each store, product and vendor kept once in its own table (sales records refer to them by number), so a correction made there applies to every record.SQL run by load_data.py (raw, curate)
Removed 1,512,965 rows the state's export repeats verbatim, and 13,258 zero records (likely cancelled). detailsSQL in load_data.py (clean)
Linked each product's old product IDs to its current one, so sales recorded under an old ID count toward the same product. detailsPython + SQL in load_data.py (clean)
Counted each store in its current city and county for its whole history (a few stores moved or were re-recorded over the years).SQL in load_data.py (curate)
After the request: shaping the data for this forecast
The AI wrote one SQL query that selects the sales records for this request: which products, which stores, and the dollars on each record (see The SQL as run).the AI (Claude), checked by dod/sqlcheck.py
Computed monthly sums of the selected records for each series and each store (calendar months), complete months only. A month with no orders counts as 0, since the warehouse was checked to have orders in every month from Jan 2016 to Aug 2026; months before the first sale are left blank.dod/history.py (SQL + Python)
Derived new features for every month, including the months being forecast (the Which inputs helped figure shows which ones the forecast uses): time of year: where the period falls in the year. Ridge regression sees the sine and cosine of the date, a smooth wave that repeats every year so that December sits next to January; LightGBM sees the month number, 1 to 12; business days and holidays: business days in each month (weekdays minus federal holidays), and four flags for whether Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day or July 4th falls in it; county population: Census population of the counties this forecast's stores are in; active stores: how many stores ordered the product in the 12 months before each month, counted one forecast horizon earlier, so the count is always known when the forecast is made.dod/features.py (Python)
Standardized for the models: each series and input scaled to mean 0, spread 1 before fitting, and predictions scaled back.dod/model.py (Python)

How the model was chosen

How this forecast is made. Each month's forecast comes from this model. It was picked by re-tuning on the Testing period (Sep 2024 to Aug 2026), with models trained on earlier months only: its total misses there were 0.75 times those of last year alone (smaller is better; 1.00 = as good as last year). Tuning on the Tuning period (Sep 2022 to Aug 2024) chose a ridge regression, which was then 18% more accurate than last year alone in the Testing period (Sep 2024 to Aug 2026), months it never saw: that is where this page's accuracy figures come from.

How the mix with last year was chosen

Each month's forecast can blend the models' forecast with simply repeating the same month last year. 10 blends were tried (the best model or the average of the best 3; 0% to 100% weight on the models) and scored on the Testing period, as their misses divided by last year's: 1.000 = as good as last year, smaller is better. The best blend, marked below, is used.

Inputs. Besides its own past sales, the model can learn from time of year, business days and holidays, county population and active stores (described under How the data was prepared). Each was tried with and without on the Testing period and kept only if it made the forecast better. This forecast uses time of year, business days and holidays and active stores. Note: the accuracy figures at the top come from an earlier round of tuning (Sep 2022 to Aug 2024), so they are measured on months that tuning never saw; that round used business days and holidays, county population and active stores.

What the agent did

How the AI agent (Claude) turned the request into what “Read as” shows at the top. It writes the SQL that selects the sales records (which products, which stores, which measure) and names the time grain. Fixed code then checks that the SQL can only read data, never change it; sums the selected records into monthly totals for each series; picks and tests the model; and generates this page.

The agent's toolbox. The AI agent (Claude Sonnet 5) does text-to-SQL. To turn words like “cream liqueur” or “Des Moines” into the warehouse's own codes it has 3 tools: search the names of products, categories, vendors, stores and places; run a small test query; and, in a live session, ask the requester one clarifying question when a request is ambiguous. None of them can change the data. It then writes one SQL query that selects the sales records to forecast (instructions, tools).

The agent's rules and business definitions

Part of its instructions for every request: three rules for this warehouse's traps, and the company's definitions of common business words.

## Rules for this warehouse (follow them exactly)
1. Products: never filter order lines on item_no alone. Products were renumbered over the years; select the product's
   whole family: il.item_no IN (SELECT item_no FROM sales.item WHERE family_item_no IN (...)).
2. A brand (every size and flavor): match ALL the brand's words anywhere in the family's current name, not as a
   prefix (barrel picks are named e.g. 'BP CROWN ROYAL ...'): il.item_no IN (SELECT i.item_no FROM sales.item i JOIN
   sales.item h ON h.item_no = i.family_item_no WHERE h.item_desc ILIKE '%CROWN%' AND h.item_desc ILIKE '%ROYAL%').
3. Categories: never use invoice_line.category_code (codes were reassigned in 2016). Use today's category of the
   product: il.item_no IN (SELECT item_no FROM sales.item WHERE category_current IN (...)).

## Business definitions (the company's dictionary; follow them unless the user says otherwise)
- A brand (e.g. Hawkeye Vodka, Crown Royal) means every product of that brand: all sizes, flavors, packs and barrel
  picks.
- A spirit type (whiskey, vodka, American vodka, rum, ...) means its own categories, flavored ones included (American
  vodka includes American Flavored Vodka), but not liqueurs or ready-to-drink cocktails made from it: whiskey does not
  include Whiskey Liqueur (e.g. Fireball). Select the categories by name, never by a typed list of codes, e.g. whiskey:
  il.item_no IN (SELECT i.item_no FROM sales.item i JOIN sales.category c ON c.category_code = i.category_current
  WHERE c.category_name ILIKE '%WHISK%' AND c.category_name NOT ILIKE '%LIQUEUR%').
- Sizes go by bottle size, not by words in the product name: minis are 50 ml, pints 375 ml, fifths 750 ml, liters
  1000 ml, handles 1750 ml. Use the product family's size: h.bottle_volume_ml with h the family's current item.
- A vendor's products (e.g. all Diageo products) means the order lines that vendor sold (l.vendor_no), not the
  products it owns today: brands change hands.
- A period named by an event or season means through its end: "for the holidays" is through December 31.

How it knows the tables and columns. At the start of every request the agent reads the warehouse's data dictionary from the database: 12 tables and 72 columns. Its search tools then find the actual names below. This forecast's data came from two of the tables:

tableused forwhat the agent is told about it
sales.invoice_lineread by the AI's queryOne row per product line on a retailer's wholesale liquor order from the state (Iowa Class E licensees), 2016 onward, cleaned (see meta.data_fixes). Price, pack and category_code are as recorded on the order date.
sales.storeread by the AI's queryLicensed retail stores that ordered liquor. Attributes are the most recently recorded values.

What it did, step by step:

  1. Searched cities for “Ankeny”: found Ankeny (Polk County, 48 stores).
  2. Searched stores for “Hy-Vee Ankeny”: found Hy-Vee Food Store #2 / State Ankeny, Hy-Vee Wine And Spirits (1022) / Ankeny, Hy-Vee C-Store #2 - Ankeny and 1 more.
  3. Searched stores for “Costco Ankeny”: found Costco Wholesale #1630 / Ankeny.
  4. Ran a read-only query: SELECT CASE WHEN s.store_name ILIKE '%HY-VEE%' THEN 'Hy-Vee' WHEN s.store_name ILIKE '%COSTCO%' THEN 'Costco' ELSE 'All
  5. Submitted its SQL selecting the sales records; fixed code checked it is one read-only SELECT with the right columns.

Exactly what ran

Agent: claude-sonnet-5, 4 API calls, 19,224 input tokens (11,493 read from cache) and 1,485 output tokens, about $0.04, 18s of agent time.

What ran: the AI's SQL selecting the sales records, then fixed code for everything after it.

The SQL as run

Written by the AI, checked to be one read-only SELECT, and run under a read-only database login, inside fixed code's own sums (by month, store and product). It selected 582,337 sales records (Jan 2016 through Aug 2026).

SELECT l.ordered_on AS day, l.store_no AS store_no, l.item_no AS item_no,
  CASE WHEN s.store_name ILIKE '%HY-VEE%' THEN 'Hy-Vee'
       WHEN s.store_name ILIKE '%COSTCO%' THEN 'Costco'
       ELSE 'All other stores' END AS series,
  l.sales_dollars AS value
FROM sales.invoice_line l
JOIN sales.store s ON s.store_no = l.store_no
WHERE s.city = 'ANKENY'
  AND l.ordered_on >= '2016-01-01'
Data: Iowa Liquor Sales, State of Iowa, via the Iowa Data Hub, CC BY 4.0; modified (duplicates removed, aggregated). Census population: U.S. Census Bureau. Not endorsed by the State of Iowa. Orders through 2026-08-31.
